Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: World Bank diagnostic notes KONTAKTU as a government initiative for automated tax filing and payments (70+ firms), indicating partial digital revenue collection capability.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Partial. DGCI's Kontaktu portal (verified live, Dec 2025) allows online payment of most taxes, contributions and fees via bank transfer or Orange/MTN mobile money, but customs duties are handled separately by the customs authority and are not confirmed as payable via Kontaktu, so 'Partial' (not 'Yes') remains the correct score.

Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: World Bank diagnostic explicitly mentions “promising initiatives for automated tax filing and payments” (KONTAKTU), but does not confirm a fully operational nationwide tax portal for all taxpayers; scored as under development.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: Upgraded from Under development to Yes. Kontaktu (kontaktu.mef.gw) is DGCI's official, currently operational tax e-filing and e-payment portal, verified live, supporting IGV, DECIRF, DRE and DCI declarations plus a 'Pagamento simplificado' e-payment route via bank transfer, Orange Money or MTN, including QR-code payment. A December 2025 DGCI service instruction (Instrução de Serviço Nº 25/GDGCI/2025) makes Kontaktu the mandatory system for taxpayer registration (NIF), evidencing active operational status rather than development.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross‑border transfers exist but are limited: World Bank diagnostic shows cross‑border mobile money was only ~1% of 2020 mobile money transactions; Orange Money/MTN corridors and WAEMU regional systems support some cross‑border functionality but not demonstrated as fully functional, ubiquitous cross‑border instant payments.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Partially functional. Guinea-Bissau is part of the WAEMU STAR-UEMOA/SICA-UEMOA regional payment systems, which provide genuine cross-border settlement within the 8-country union (BCEAO's 2022-2023 payment systems report shows growing intra-UEMOA transaction volumes). Separately, PAPSS's June 2026 network coverage document lists Guinea-Bissau as reachable only via its 'Extended Network' for inbound mobile-wallet payments, with full participant status still 'live soon' — so broader Pan-African cross-border functionality remains partial rather than fully functional.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: World Bank diagnostic references pilots/initiatives around salary e‑payments (e.g., COVID Commission) but does not provide evidence of broad, active G2P digitization; treated as limited use.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded from Limited Use to Yes - Active Use. The IMF confirms (29 May 2024) that Guinea-Bissau's Ministries of Finance and Public Administration launched a blockchain platform monitoring the real-time disbursement of public salaries and pensions by commercial banks, evidencing an established, government-wide digital G2P payment pipeline for the civil service wage bill. However, the IMF's June 2025 Selected Issues Paper notes that social-transfer programmes beyond salaries/pensions remain nascent and largely donor-funded, so coverage is uneven across G2P categories — recommend human review to confirm whether Active Use should be scoped narrowly to salaries/pensions.

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: World Bank diagnostic reports low but existing e‑payments/merchant ecosystem (e.g., 304 merchants registered for e‑payments; few active), and mobile money includes ‘payments’ use case share (4% of 2020 transactions), indicating P2B functionality exists (even if limited adoption).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Yes. Orange's official developer documentation lists Guinea-Bissau among countries where Orange Money Web Payment/M-Payment is available to merchants for e-commerce and bill payments, and local reporting (O Democrata, 24 May 2023) confirms Orange Bissau launched a QR-code Orange Money card enabling in-person merchant payments. This is fresher, more direct evidence of P2B functionality than the 2021 World Bank diagnostic alone.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: No credible evidence found of widespread, active digital P2G payments (taxes/fees) for individuals; World Bank diagnostic mentions KONTAKTU tax e‑filing/payments expansion to firms but not clear for individual P2G. Scored as limited use.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded from Limited Use to Yes - Active Use. Kontaktu allows individual taxpayers to file declarations (e.g. DECIRF for withheld personal income) and pay taxes, contributions and fees electronically via bank transfer, Orange Money or MTN Mobile Money, including a 'Pagamento simplificado' route usable without a Kontaktu account and by QR code. Its continued, mandatory use for taxpayer registration as of December 2025 indicates active, not merely limited, take-up, though usage is likely concentrated among the formal taxpayer base rather than the general population.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: BCEAO states it is responsible for management of WAEMU payment systems including SICA‑UEMOA (automated clearing) and STAR‑UEMOA (RTGS), including operational and technical management, risk management, reporting and invoicing, indicating central bank direct operation of core payment system infrastructure for member states including Guinea‑Bissau.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Direct Operation. BCEAO's own payment-systems-management page was fetched and verified: it directly operates SICA-UEMOA (clearing) and STAR-UEMOA (RTGS), including operational/technical management, risk management and invoicing, for all WAEMU member states including Guinea-Bissau. Source content matches the stated score exactly; no change needed.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: World Bank Guinea‑Bissau Digital Economy Country Assessment provides detailed mobile money and payment system statistics (e.g., 2020 mobile money transactions 22.47M; value XOF 146B), but this is not published as routine BCEAO dashboard reporting for the country; evidence supports at least ad hoc public reporting via major diagnostic report.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded from Ad Hoc to Annual. BCEAO publishes a recurring 'Rapport sur les infrastructures de marchés financiers, les moyens et les services de paiement de l'UEMOA' (most recent edition covering 2022-2023, published April 2025) and a predecessor annual payment systems report dating back to at least 2017, with detailed regional transaction volume/value and participant statistics covering all WAEMU members including Guinea-Bissau. This is a genuine recurring public report, not merely the ad hoc World Bank diagnostic previously cited.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Most recent quantified evidence found: World Bank diagnostic reports 1.7M mobile money accounts at end‑2020 (population ~2M) and 22.47M mobile money transactions in 2020; this suggests broad access but does not equal active users share. With limited demand-side Findex data available, scored as 20–49% to be conservative.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Downgraded from 20-49% to <20%, but flagged for human review. The 2021-2022 national harmonised household survey (World Bank microdata, Inquérito Harmonizado) shows only 6.8% of respondents reporting 'Mobile Banking' use, and the World Bank's 2021 diagnostic notes that around 43% of Bissau-Guineans remained entirely excluded from any financial account. Neither source precisely matches the indicator's 90-day 'digital payment transaction' definition, so this figure should be checked against Global Findex 2025 country-level data (not available in searches conducted) before being finalised.
